title: Break-Even: Where Revenue Catches Total Cost
subject: business-studies

scenes.caption: Axes first, then the flat fixed-cost line
scenes.narration: Rent and insurance cost $2,000 however much the business makes. Watch the marker sweep across: output rises, but the fixed-cost line never leaves $2,000, because fixed costs do not change with output.

scenes.caption: Total cost starts at fixed costs, then rises
scenes.narration: Total cost does not start at zero: at zero output the business still owes the $2,000 fixed costs. From that intercept the line rises only by the $10 variable cost of each unit made, as the marker climbs it.

steps.text: Total cost starts at $2,000, then rises

scenes.caption: Revenue rises faster, but still in loss
scenes.narration: Total revenue starts at zero and rises faster, at $20 per unit, but at low output it is still below total cost. Follow the marker sweeping up: the shaded gap between the lines is the loss made at that output.

steps.text: Below break-even, total cost is above revenue

scenes.caption: Break-even, then the profit zone opens
scenes.narration: At 200 units the lines cross: total revenue equals total cost at $4,000, so there is no profit and no loss. Sweep past it and revenue pulls above total cost - the loss zone closes and the profit zone opens, with only one crossing.
